findings.what: c4_mutations m2 ('generator: the incremental DAG skips the cycle test') is caught only by a runaway, never by a failing assertion
findings.evidence: pass 1: under m2 the C4 suites' xctest grew to a 4.47 GB footprint and was killed by tools/memguard.sh at 13:48:09 (build/memguard.log: 'killed python pid 2900 footprint 4471 MB: .../xctest -XCTest PathCoreTests.C4FullSolverTests/...'); the script then reports plain 'CAUGHT' with no failing test named (build/p/V1/core/run-1/mutations-c4.txt: '2 CAUGHT ... []'). pass 2: the same mutant ran 600 s without a result and the harness killed its whole process tree at 17:06:49 (build/p/V1/core/mut/c4-r2/harness.log: 'TIMEOUT after 600 s ... killed tree [49114, 49126]'; no orphan left; run-2/mutations-c4.txt: '2 CAUGHT (the suite hangs: killed after 600 s)'; its test log mut/c4-r2/logs/006-test.log has no test output). B0 on 09-28 saw the same 600 s hang (build/p/B0/logs/mutations-1.log). The c4 script counts a hang as a catch by design; soc_mutations.py's rule ('a hang is a defect to fix, not a catch') would call it NOT JUDGED. Every other mutant of every script (155 of 156 per pass) fails by a named failing assertion.
findings.fix_hint: Add a bounded GeneratorTests case that performs one head flip closing a cycle on a tiny board and asserts the incremental DAG refuses it (and one that a non-cycling flip is accepted), so m2 fails by assertion in seconds instead of by runaway memory.

findings.what: tools/memguard.sh classifies an xctest as python when its -XCTest list names a test containing 'Python' (e.g. testNegativeControlsAreCaughtWithThePythonMessages) followed by an apps/mazeout path, so the 3 GB python limit applies instead of the 6 GB xctest limit
findings.evidence: build/memguard.log 09-29 13:48:09 'killed python pid 2900 footprint 4471 MB: /Applications/Xcode.app/.../xctest -XCTest PathCoreTests.C4FullSolverTests/testEveryShippedLevel,...' — the case pattern *[Pp]ython*apps/mazeout* matched the xctest command line. Harmless here (the process was a runaway mutant), but a legitimate heavy PathCore test run between 3 and 6 GB would be killed.
findings.fix_hint: In tools/memguard.sh put the *xctest* case before the python case (or match the executable name via ps -o comm=) — orchestrator's tool, not edited by V1-core.
findings.status: FIXED by the orchestrator at 13:59 (build/blocked.md: memguard now goes by the executable, xctest limit 6 GB); pass 2 confirms it: the same runaway mutant then ran to the harness 600 s timeout instead of a 3 GB kill.
